title: New balance keys load via permissive jint — fractional/overflow values silently coerce past the documented fail-fast
evidence: core/catalog.odin:487-493: `b.lane_queue_packets = jint(obj, "lane_queue_packets", 0)` / `if b.lane_queue_packets <= 0 { return {"balance.json", "lane_queue_packets", "lane_queue_packets must be > 0 (per-lane queue bound, E9)"} }` / `b.pool_max_packets = jint(obj, "pool_max_packets", 0)` / `if b.pool_max_packets <= 0 { return {"balance.json", "pool_max_packets", "pool_max_packets must be > 0 (in-flight pool cap, E22)"} }`. jint (catalog.odin:676-681): `case json.Integer: return i32(x)` / `case json.Float:   return i32(x)`. Verified with the pinned toolchain (odin dev-2026-08-nightly): `i32(4294967302) = 6` (i64 wrap), `i32(6.9) = 6` (float truncation), and json.parse(parse_integers=true) yields Integer for 4294967302 / Float for 6.9 — so `"lane_queue_packets": 6.9`, `"lane_queue_packets": 4294967302`, and the wrapped-negative `"pool_max_packets": -4294967290` all load as 6 and PASS the `<= 0` guard. The two keys are the only 3.3 additions; every other new sim field since 3.1 (packet_types, demand, lane_preset weights) rejects non-integers via jint_strict / `.(json.Integer)`.
detail: The new catalog boundary accepts values the file does not state: 6.9 truncates to 6 and 2^32+6 wraps to 6, silently diverging from authoring intent; a wrapped negative bypasses the documented 'must be > 0' fail-fast (ODN-5). Effective bound stays >= 1, so no crash/unsafety — a hardening gap.
recommended_fix: Load both keys with jint_strict (rejects json.Float) and range-check before the cast (reject outside 1..i32::max), matching the packet_types/demand loaders' 'sim fields must be integers' bar.
